value.title: Canonical problem
value.currentStateSummary: Two accepted structural results are now organized under distinct active directions. First, deterministic finite-block private-message codes induce an exact dependence-balance defect bound, a fixed-map single-coordinate law, and four compatible rate rows, but with blocklength-dependent auxiliary alphabets. Second, an explicit finite entropic witness shows that the specified coarse dependence-balance relaxation cannot be lowered below 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 by universal finite-variable information inequalities or any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions. The latter witness is not a binary-input BSSC distribution, so these results neither establish a new capacity bound nor rule out exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific refinements.
value.localResidualSummary: Remaining work includes a structure-preserving cardinality or compactness reduction for code-induced laws, certified global optimization of a valid converse, and BSSC-specific posterior-consistency or direct code inequalities capable of excluding the nonbinary entropy witness and improving the certified converse.

value.title: Code-induced converse structure
value.objective: Develop rigorous converse constraints directly inherited from finite-block private-message codes and determine whether they admit a structure-preserving finite-dimensional reduction.
value.currentStateSummary: An exact finite-block dependence telescope, separate Fano endpoint bounds, a fixed-encoder-map induced law, and four compatible rate rows are established for deterministic private-message codes over finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channels. The resulting auxiliaries can grow with blocklength, so this does not yet furnish a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region or a numerical capacity improvement.
value.localResidualSummary: Find a valid support, cardinality, or compactness reduction preserving message/time independence, the fixed encoder map, dependence balance, and all four rate rows; then certify any resulting global converse optimization or derive a stronger channel-specific inequality.

value.title: Entropy-relaxation obstructions and channel-specific refinements
value.objective: Determine which converse refinements survive exact entropic counterexamples and identify channel-specific consistency constraints that can exclude them.
value.currentStateSummary: For the specified coarse uniform-input BSSC entropy relaxation incorporating exact dependence balance, all conditional BEC identities, and two sharp scalar support inequalities, an actual finite entropic witness attains both direct-sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. Universal finite-variable information inequalities and finite standard copy-lemma hierarchies cannot remove this witness. Its input variable is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components rather than an actual binary BSSC input.
value.localResidualSummary: Develop exact jointly consistent binary-posterior, transition-law, or direct multiletter code constraints that exclude the witness, and determine whether such constraints can produce a certified converse improvement. The obstruction alone supplies no broadcast-channel capacity bound.

value.title: Finite-block code-induced dependence balance and compatible rate rows
value.statement: Let A and B be independent uniform private messages of sizes N_1,N_2≥2, deterministically encoded over n uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channel, with receiver errors p_1,p_2. Define F_j=h_2(p_j)+p_j log_2(N_j-1), δ_j=F_j/n, and S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n). Then the exact identity Σ_i[I(A;B|S_i,Y_i)-I(A;B|S_i,Z_i)]=I(A;B|Y^n)-I(A;B|Z^n), together with separate Fano bounds on the two nonnegative endpoints, implies that uniform independent time T and U=A, V=B, W=S_T, X=X_T satisfy |I(U;V|W,T,Y)-I(U;V|W,T,Z)|≤max{δ_1,δ_2}. Their complete induced law has the fixed-map factorization p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=n^{-1}p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w|u,v,t)1{x=f_t(u,v)}P_{YZ|X}(y,z|x), so W cannot select another encoder after (u,v,t) is fixed. With R_j=n^{-1}log_2 N_j, the same variables satisfy R_1≤I(U,W;Y|T)+δ_1, R_2≤I(V,W;Z|T)+δ_2, R_1+R_2≤I(U,W;Y|T)+I(X;Z|U,W,T)+δ_1+δ_2, and R_1+R_2≤I(V,W;Z|T)+I(X;Y|V,W,T)+δ_1+δ_2. This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition for the stated deterministic codes, not a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
scopeQualifications: The displayed Fano expression is literal for message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2; singleton messages require a separate harmless convention.
The conclusion is stated for deterministic private-message codes over finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channels.
The message and W alphabets may grow with blocklength, so no fixed-cardinality auxiliary reduction or single-letter outer region is established.
No numerical BSSC capacity bound or improvement of an existing certified upper bound follows from this result alone.

proofs: Chain-rule and conditioned Csiszár-sum derivations of the two individual-rate and two sum-rate rows, retaining only explicitly nonnegative remainders.
Exact telescoping of D_i=I(A;B|Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n), followed by separate Fano bounds on the two endpoint conditional mutual informations.
methods: Uniform-time single-coordinate extraction with the full fixed-encoder-map factorization retained.

value.title: Exact entropic obstruction to the specified universal-inequality and copy refinement route
value.statement: At uniform input, let h=h_2(1/4), c=h-1/2, and r=h-3/4. For the specified coarse relaxation imposing the seven common-noise BSSC entropies, message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map and memoryless Markov equalities, exact dependence balance, every conditional BEC identity I(L;Y,Z|K)=1/2 I(L;X|K) for disjoint subtuples L,K⊆{U,V,W,T} with L nonempty, and the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side r, there is an actual finite entropic distribution for which both direct-sum branches equal 2h_2(1/4)-5/4=0.3725562489182657…. Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot lower this relaxation below that value. Nor can any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions, because each copy step can be realized by conditional resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and objective.
scopeQualifications: This is an obstruction to the specified coarse entropy/universal-inequality/finite-copy refinement route, not a broadcast-channel capacity bound.
The witness is an actual finite distribution but not an actual binary-input BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.
Exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude the displayed witness and remain viable refinement routes.
The result applies at uniform input and only to the stated relaxation, including its particular base entropies, structural equalities, BEC identities, and two scalar support inequalities.
No achievability result, global converse optimization, capacity formula, or improvement of an existing certified upper bound is established.

proofs: Calculus proof of the sharp scalar posterior-support constant r using the global supporting tangent to the BSSC information-difference function.
Conditional-resampling realization of each standard copy-lemma step, showing preservation of the finite witness marginal and objective through every finite copy sequence.

Explicit construction from mutually independent binary components with prescribed affine-in-h entropies, yielding the required base entropy vector, structural equalities, exact dependence balance, all conditional BEC identities, both scalar support equalities, and both objective values.
methods: Exact component-set entropy accounting for tuple-valued random variables.
Finite-distribution realization of copy extensions by conditional resampling.
computations: Standard-library exact affine-in-h checker verifies positivity of component entropies, the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, both zero dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both sharp support rows, and both objective branches.
tools: Python 3 standard-library exact symbolic checker using rational affine expressions in h.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted compound assessment contains two independently reusable results with distinct downstream roles: a code-induced finite-block converse constraint and a no-go theorem for one entropy/copy refinement route. They are placed in separate durable child programs because future support-reduction work and future channel-specific witness-exclusion work are independently pursuable. The no-go result depends on the code-induced dependence-balance structure. No existing intermediate result was available for consolidation, and the root is refreshed only as their ancestor.

topologyRationale: Create two durable child programs and one reciprocal intermediate result in each, with an acyclic dependency from the entropy/copy obstruction to the finite-block dependence-balance result. No existing entity is moved, retired, split, or merged.
